ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: High-intensity white and light-grey pixels occupy approximately 55-60% of the visible surface area, while low-intensity black and dark-grey pixels occupy the remaining 40-45%, primarily concentrated in the central isthmus and trailing edge borders.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Large high-intensity (white) contiguous regions are located on the distal portions of both the left and right lobes. These are bisected by a low-intensity (black) vertical band at the median notch. trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: The central depression is a sharp V-shaped notch with an internal angle estimated at approximately 42 degrees and a shallow depth relative to the total horizontal span of the fluke.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, high-amplitude serrations are visible across the entire trailing edge. trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: The leading edges exhibit a convex sweep that tapers into highly irregular, jagged trajectories along the trailing edges of both lobes.

localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: A series of three distinct, roughly parallel dark linear pixel disruptions (rake marks) are visible on the distal left lobe, oriented diagonally from the outer edge toward the center.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Heavy biological encrustation (barnacle colonies) is visible as high-relief, irregular texture on the outer tips of both the left and right lobes. Numerous depigmented circular lesions are scattered across the ventral surface.
